# SVG fixtures

These original SVG files exercise the LVGL SVG parser and vector renderer. `expected.json` stores row-major RGBA pixel bounds after source-over compositing on `[16, 32, 48]`, with one four-channel array per pixel. File hashes identify the input bytes. Expected values come from geometric areas and color equations; no framebuffer output is used as a reference.

`geometry.svg` applies a 32×24 viewport to `viewBox="0 0 16 12"` with `preserveAspectRatio="none"`, then translates its group by `(1, 1)`. The rectangle occupies `[4, 14) × [4, 10)`. The right triangle has vertices `(4, 12)`, `(16, 12)`, and `(4, 24)`; pixels on its integer diagonal have exactly half coverage. `geometry-viewbox-first.svg` changes attribute order. `geometry-long-header.svg` adds an ignored 600-character attribute before dimensions and viewBox. All three have identical expected pixels.

`fills.svg` places two paths with same-direction nested rectangular contours. Nonzero fills both contours; evenodd removes the inner rectangle. Coverage is exactly zero or one because every edge is on an integer pixel boundary. The vector backend converts solid opacity with `floor(255 × opacity / 256)`. Opaque paint uses 254; `fill-opacity=".5"` first truncates to 127, then converts to 126. The color reference is `floor((foreground × alpha + background × (255 − alpha)) / 255)`. Painted solid pixels allow one channel level for integer raster/compositing quantization.

`gradient.svg` fills `[4, 28) × [4, 20)` with a horizontal objectBoundingBox gradient. Its stops are `[220, 40, 20, 63]` and `[20, 100, 220, 223]`; the alpha values are the truncated SVG opacities `.25 × 255` and `.875 × 255`. Straight color and alpha interpolate independently at pixel centers using `t = (x + .5 − 4) / 24`, followed by the same source-over equation. The three-level channel allowance is shared with the vector gradient tests and covers the native gradient lookup table, 8-bit interpolation, premultiplication, and composition stages; it does not allow geometry shifts. Gradient transform, spread modes, extra stops, and SVG text are outside these fixtures.

`quadratic.svg` and `cubic.svg` describe the same parabola with paths `M2 12 Q8 0 14 12 Z` and `M2 12 C6 4 10 4 14 12 Z`. Their pixel geometry matches the 16-pixel outline in `../freetype-outline/expected.json`. The reference imports that file's analytically integrated `coverage_min` and `coverage_max`, including the proved chord and intersection error bounds; its hash is recorded in `expected.json`. Coverage is multiplied by `254 / 255`, then composited using `[224, 192, 160]`. Colors inside the geometric enclosure allow two levels. The two SVG files therefore test quadratic/cubic parsing against a shared mathematical boundary.

Pixels outside the reference's painted region must remain exact background, including pixels outside the source dimensions. Tests exercise synchronous document loading and deletion, copied vector tasks, file-source dimensions, resource copies, source replacement, repeated rendering, and variable-source descriptors whose XML remains alive until image deletion. Rendering uses the native LVGL SVG path and does not require ThorVG's SVG loader.

`empty-self-closing.svg` and `empty-closed.svg` are valid 32×24 documents containing no paths; their reference is entirely background. The five `rejected` fixtures contain a wrong root name, mismatched group, unclosed root, two root elements, or truncated opening root. Each must return a null DOM, fail file information lookup, clear an image's source, and leave the framebuffer unchanged. A valid replacement is rendered after each failure in the same runtime. These cases check defined parser failures; they do not establish acceptance or rejection of every SVG/XML construct.
